name: MN-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: Emmer's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising edge ($10.7M raised vs. $691K for Chapin)
Prediction markets price Democratic upset chances at only a few percent
No public polling or expert ratings indicate a competitive race
model.rationale: Emmer combines a double-digit partisan lean, entrenched incumbency, and a massive financial advantage, while prediction markets and the absence of any polling or expert attention point the same direction. Chapin's modest fundraising leaves him little capacity to change the race's fundamentals.
model.watch: A decisive national wave against Republicans or an unexpected scandal involving Emmer would be the most plausible path to narrowing this margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minnesota's 6th District leans firmly Republican, and Tom Emmer has held the seat since 2015, winning comfortably in each cycle. He is seeking another term against Democrat Doug Chapin, who works in election administration. Emmer has raised more than $10.7 million with $3.7 million still on hand, while Chapin has raised about $691,000 with under $100,000 available. No public polls of the race have been released, and no major expert ratings list it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset, and the district's partisan lean plus Emmer's incumbency and financial edge point the same direction. Chapin would need a large national wave or an unexpected shift locally to close a double-digit gap. Barring a significant change in the political environment, the seat remains firmly in Republican hands.
